$comment: Twin pairs that currently differ SEMANTICALLY, comment-only and seam-import
differences excluded, per scripts/check-twin-inventory.mjs's comparison, which
this record imports rather than restating.
A RATCHET: the set may shrink, never grow. A pair appearing here that was not
here before is a regression, and `--record` REFUSES to write a grown set, so
the command the failure message suggests cannot be used to make the failure go
away. Locking in a convergence is the only edit it will make.
The denominator has its own floor, and it is NOT in this file:
`EXAMINED_FLOOR` in scripts/check-twin-drift-ratchet.mjs. Shrinking the twin
roster would shrink this set too, and read as progress.
Four entries below are hand-added, not `--record` output, and this paragraph
is their stated reason. Two are myne-md/myne#697:
`src/components/settings/MemorySection.tsx::mobile/src/app/flows/MemorySection.tsx`
and `src/notes/components/MemoryPopover.tsx::mobile/src/app/flows/MemorySheet.tsx`.
Both are new twin pairs with recorded per-client posture (desktop Settings
section and popover against mobile flow and bottom sheet); the divergence is
legitimate growth, not a regression cover. The third is myne-md/myne#768:
`src/lib/personAccount.ts::mobile/src/lib/personAccount.ts`. Desktop's wrapper
is async and carries AcceptedInviteView; mobile's is a sync port of the same
six `sync_person_*` commands plus PersonStatusView, so
the two genuinely differ past comments while the command names are one answer.
The fourth is myne-md/myne#851 task 15, and it DOES grow the set by one pair:
`src/lib/memberNames.ts::mobile/src/lib/memberNames.ts`. Both sides are new
files in that change rather than a pair that drifted apart, so there is no
convergence being unlocked: both are the per-client `invoke` binding for the
shared `myne-core` `vault.member-names` store, and both import the wire-shape
mirror and the refusal-to-copy mapper from `@myne/client-core` rather than
holding a copy, so what is left here is transport and cannot converge: desktop
wraps two commands because its Members-list row editor renames and clears,
mobile wraps only the setter because post-onboarding editing is out of task
15's scope and `scripts/check-ipc-binding-callers.mjs` refuses a binding no
production code calls. The divergence is a recorded per-client surface, not a
regression cover. All four are classified in scripts/check-twin-inventory.mjs,
and `--record` still refuses any further growth; the three before the fourth
left this set unchanged, and that fourth was the first hand edit this file records; the five below follow it, each with its reason.

The next three are myne-md/myne#849 (`mobile-live-presence`), hand-added rather than `--record` output, and the paragraph above is their stated reason. All three are new twin pairs rather than pairs that drifted apart, so nothing converges by adding them, and each is a case where the divergence is the design rather than debt. `src/lib/live.ts::mobile/src/lib/live.ts` and `src/lib/identity.ts::mobile/src/lib/identity.ts` are per-client TRANSPORT BINDINGS: one `invoke` wrapper each over the same shared-core commands (`live_session_*` over `myne_core::plugins::live`, and `resolve_identity`), differing only in the import specifiers each tree must reach through its own platform seam, with the identity pair's type import going through the `@myne/resolved-identity` alias so the Rust wire mirror is not retyped. Neither file holds an answer, which is why the twin inventory records both as `delegated`. `src/platform/capabilities.ts::mobile/src/platform/capabilities.ts` is the pair whose divergence IS the decision: a capability descriptor answers "does THIS client provide X", so two agreeing answer sets would be the defect. What moved in that change is the layer above it, the VOCABULARY (`Capability` and the keyed `CAPABILITY_KEYS` record) into `@myne/client-core`, so mobile could answer the closed list at all; before the move the union sat in a file the phone cannot compile, and the desktop module's own claim that the closure forced every implementation to answer was true of exactly one client. The reasons the pairs differ are recorded per pair in `scripts/check-twin-inventory.mjs` and the structure is `design-notes/clients/0716`.

The last two are hand-added for myne-md/myne#849 from the review round that found them MISSING, which is worth stating: task 11's own What-to-build named both pairs ("the desktop presence roster against the mobile sheet, and the two policy shims") and the first pass classified only the four the path sweep could see, so two cross-path pairs shipped unrostered (the `check-twin-inventory.mjs` roster gained them in the same act). Both are new pairs rather than drift: `src/notes/components/WhoIsHereTab.tsx` against `mobile/src/app/flows/editor/sheets/PresenceSheet.tsx` is a `screen` pair, because the store and the label rule are one shared implementation while the container is a right-panel tab against a bottom sheet; `src/notes/liveNote.ts` against `mobile/src/lib/liveNote.ts` is `delegated`, the per-client host wiring over the one policy module in `@myne/client-core`.

The next one is hand-added for myne-md/myne#938's review, and it is the first pair that was IDENTICAL and was made to differ: `src-tauri/src/device_key.rs::mobile/src-tauri/src/device_key.rs`. Each host installs only the device-key store its own crate contains, and the file used to name BOTH under `cfg` arms, so a desktop Windows build and a mobile Android build each carried an arm pointing at a module the other crate has. That is a compile error on targets this machine cannot build, which is why no lane caught it. The arms were removed from the side that never builds for them: desktop dropped the `device_key_keystore` arm and the fallback's `target_os = "android"` predicate, mobile dropped the `device_key_dpapi` arm and its `windows` predicate. What is left differing is exactly those two lines, and it cannot converge without inventing a module for a platform the crate never builds for. The provider contract and the fail-closed rule stay in `core/src/plugins/sync/device_identity.rs`, which is what must not drift.
The sixth and seventh are hand-added by the mobile half of myne-md/myne#535, and
both grow the set the same way the fourth did: each is a NEW pair created by that
change rather than a pair that drifted apart, so nothing converges and the hand
edit is the recorded decision rather than a cover.
`src/lib/pending-approval.ts::mobile/src/lib/pending-approval.ts` is the awaiting-
approval verdict. The mobile copy DROPS the `localOnlyVault` bail-out on purpose:
on a desktop awaiting sync approval does not block local use and the Settings
panel shows the wait, while mobile's Settings panel carries only the approver's
side of the compare, so the wait is the only surface a joining phone has left
that can show its code. The read ORDER was shared and is not any more: the
mobile copy answers the join's own marker BEFORE the baseline, because a
joined vault's first pull lands a head on the locked-to-unlocked edge and a
baseline-first verdict retired the marker that owed the compare. Desktop and web
never ask at all: their accept lands the vault on the `pending-approval` stage at
accept time (`decisions/sync/0767`), so there is no marker to order and no writer
of one.
`src/hooks/useIdleAutoLock.ts::mobile/src/hooks/useIdleAutoLock.ts` is the idle
re-lock timer, extracted from `EditorFlow`'s inline copy when the approval wait
became a second post-unlock screen that holds keys. The deadline arithmetic and
the `visibilitychange` re-evaluation are the same on both sides; only HOW the
caller locks differs, which is per-client by construction. Both are classified
in scripts/check-twin-inventory.mjs, and `--record` still refuses any further
growth.
